source.title: A note on the convergence of RED algorithms under minimal hypotheses and open questions

accepted.question_text: Consider the inverse problem y = A x̂ + e, where x̂ belongs to a low-dimensional model set Σ, A is a linear measurement map, and e is noise. Let P_Σ be a generalized projection onto Σ with the restricted β-Lipschitz property: for every z, every x in Σ, and every u in P_Σ(z), ||u − x||₂ ≤ β ||z − x||₂. The modified RED iteration is z_n = (1 − λ)x_n + λP_Σ(x_n), followed by x_{n+1} = z_n − μAᵀ(Az_n − y). A convergence bound is known when Σ is proximinal and P_Σ is close to the orthogonal projection P_Σ^⊥, specifically ||P_Σ − P_Σ^⊥||₂ ≤ η. Can one prove convergence of this modified RED iteration to a stable solution when P_Σ is only a generic restricted-Lipschitz projection, without assuming orthogonality or approximate orthogonality of the projection, as in the generalized projected-gradient-descent setting?

evidence.quote: In this note we show convergence of a slightly modified version of the RED algorithm under similar (stronger) hypotheses, and we ask open questions arising from these results.
Then P has the restricted β-Lipschitz property with respect to Σ iff for all z ∈ RN, x ∈ Σ, u ∈ P(z), we have ||u − x||2 ≤ β ||z − x||2.

We propose to look at the following modified RED algorithm, we keep the same definition of zn but calculate the gradient step in zn instead of xn: zn = (1 − λ)xn + λPΣ(xn) ∈ [xn, PΣ(xn)] xn+1 = zn − μAT(Azn − y).

Suppose Σ is a proximinal set. Consider modified RED iterations (11) with ||PΣ − P⊥Σ||2 ≤ η. Let β = βΣ(PΣ) and δ = δΣ(μATA). Suppose r = (δβ + |1 − λ| ||I − μATA||op) < 1, then ||xn − x̂||2 ≤ rn||x0 − x̂||2 + 1/(1 − r)(|1 − λ| ||I − μATA||opη + μ ||ATe||2).
It leaves the question of convergence to a stable solution with a generic restricted Lipschitz projection without orthogonality assumption (as for GPGD).

accepted.question_text: Consider the same inverse problem y = A x̂ + e with x̂ in a model set Σ, and let P_Σ be a generalized projection onto Σ. Classical regularization by denoising (RED) uses the iteration x_{n+1} = x_n − μAᵀ(Ax_n − y) − λ(x_n − P_Σ(x_n)). Assume the measurement operator satisfies a restricted isometry condition on the secant set Σ − Σ, and assume P_Σ satisfies a restricted Lipschitz condition with respect to Σ. Is it possible to prove convergence of the classical RED iterations in this RIC-and-restricted-Lipschitz theoretical setup under conditions less restrictive than the quasi-non-expansiveness route discussed in the source, which in the orthogonal-projection and atomic-norm setting leads to a sufficient-looking condition of the form δ(μ/(λ+θ) AᵀA)β + (θ/(λ+θ))δ(μ/θ AᵀA)C_Σ ≤ 1?
accepted.context_brief: Classical RED convergence under RIC and restricted Lipschitz hypotheses

evidence.quote: Another question is to understand if another popular PnP scheme, regularization by denoising (RED) [9, 8, 10, 2] has convergence guarantees under the same minimal hypotheses. RED iterations are defined by xn+1 = xn − μAT(Axn − y) − λ(xn − PΣ(xn)).
The operator B has restricted isometry constant δ ∈ [0, 1) on the secant set Σ − Σ = {x1 − x2 : x1, x2 ∈ Σ} if for all x1, x2 ∈ Σ, ||(I − B)(x1 − x2)||2 ≤ δ||x1 − x2||2.

The main problem is that under the RIP we cannot generally bound w2 with a contractive term as u − PΣ(u) ∉ Σ − Σ. Moreover, without convexity of the model set Σ we cannot really hope to control the sign of the term ⟨u − PΣ(u), PΣ(u) − x̂⟩ if we were to develop the squared norm.
Hence quasi non-expansiveness would be achieved under the condition δ( μ/(λ + θ) ATA)β + θ/(λ + θ) δ( μ/θ ATA)CΣ ≤ 1.

This leads to following open questions. Is it possible to show convergence of the classical RED iterations with RIC and restricted Lipschitz conditions in this theoretical set-up, with less restrictive conditions?

accepted.question_text: For inverse problems y = A x̂ + e with x̂ in a low-dimensional model set Σ, generalized projected gradient descent (GPGD) uses x_{n+1} = P_Σ(x_n) − μAᵀ(AP_Σ(x_n) − y) and can stably recover x̂ with a linear rate under restricted-isometry and restricted-Lipschitz hypotheses. Modified RED reduces to GPGD when λ = 1, while other admissible λ values are described as giving slower convergence and less identifiability; the classical RED convergence route also appears to require restrictive conditions. Under what theoretical setup would the use of a classical or modified RED scheme be warranted instead of GPGD, given that RED has worse convergence-rate and identifiability properties in the analyzed setting?
accepted.context_brief: When RED is theoretically preferable to GPGD

evidence.quote: the generalized projected gradient descent (GPGD) iterations xn+1 = PΣ(xn) − μAT(APΣ(xn) − y) stably recover x̂ with linear rate
To the best of our knowledge, the RIP and restricted Lipschitz constants are the weakest known hypotheses leading to such convergence guarantees.

We see that if we chose λ = 1, we fall on GPGD iterations and obtain the same convergence rate with modified RED (under the additional orthogonality assumption of the projection). Other admissible λ lead to slower convergence (and less identifiability).

Given the results of the previous Section, what theoretical set-up would warrant the use of a (classical or modified) RED scheme instead of GPGD as convergence rates and identifiability properties are worse than GPGD?
